fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays excessive management fees, data-license royalties, or syndicated loan interest to its offshore parent at prices unrelated to market comparables, funds ongoing losses while the group earns profitability, and fails to prepare or file contemporaneous Local File, Master File and Country-by-Country reporting disclosures after exceeding the RMB 40 million to RMB 200 million statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 41 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law empowers the State Taxation Administration to adjust taxable income by reference to the arm's-length price, and the Special Tax Adjustment Measures extended the adjustment look-back to ten years in evasion cases, with compensatory interest imposed at 0.05% per day on the adjusted tax; under-declaration arising from the mispricing is sanctioned under Article 63 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law with a 50% to 500% penalty, and the adjusted transaction generates a secondary permanent establishment risk for the offshore parent in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation or approve artificial intercompany debt and fee structures are characterized as directly responsible persons in the tax adjustment procedure; personal civil liability follows under the veil-piercing doctrine for the disappointed tax debt, and where the TP manipulation constitutes intentional concealment of taxable income, Criminal Law Article 201 exposes the responsible executives to personal fines and imprisonment of up to seven years; the responsible legal representative simultaneously suffers blacklisting deposit of exit ban, and the foreign director may be barred from re-entering China until the adjusted tax and penalties are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse and Beneficial Ownership Misrepresentation (税收协定滥用与受益所有人虚假申报)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The offshore parent interposes a conduit or shell holding company with no employees, premises, or substantive activity in a lower-tax treaty jurisdiction to hold the WFOE shares, licensing rights or loan receivables, and the WFOE files treaty benefit claims with fabricated self-declarations to reduce the 10% statutory dividend, interest and royalty withholding tax to 5% or lower without genuine commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: State Taxation Administration Announcement 2018 No. 9 denies the treaty benefits for lack of beneficial ownership, requiring retroactive withholding at the full 10% statutory rate, and the erroneous treaty claim is treated as a fraudulent preferential tax position under Article 63 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law carrying a penalty of 50% to 500% of the withholding shortfall; Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law further permits a General Anti-Avoidance Rule recharacterization of the conduit structure, and Article 48 attaches a daily 0.05% surcharge to the recomputed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the legal representative who sign or endorse false beneficial ownership declarations face veil-piercing civil restitution of the full withholding shortfall and penalties from personal assets under Civil Code Article 83 and Company Law Article 20; criminal liability attaches under Criminal Law Article 201 where the underpinned withholding exceeds the criminal threshold, with imprisonment for the responsible director up to seven years and confiscation of personal property, alongside the joint-punishment blacklisting mechanism that freezes personal bank accounts, restricts first-class travel and high-consumption behavior, imposes temporary exit bans at immigration, and in serious cases allows revocation of the director's residency permission and re-entry prohibition.
